newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Legal & General to trend higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Legal & General to trend higher.

text.p: DAY'S RANGE * SUPPORT * RESTNCE* MA-25 * MA-200
+ Legal & General shares are capable of continuing their long-term uptrend and to outperform the All-Share index, technical analysts said.

+ The shares may show volatility near-term, but this would only be in keeping with the trend since the start of the year. From a longer-term perspective, the shares have made gains in a manner which suggest further potential.
Shares in insurance group Legal & General appear ready to shrug off their recent bear phase and to begin a revival or at least to outperform the market, technical analysts said.

The stock has been volatile since the start of the year -- its 10 day historic volatility has shot up to 39 percent from 10 percent at the start of the year -- but after its share price plunge in mid-March the price seems to be levelling out at 380p.
Continuing market jitters could smother any large scale strengthening of Legal & General shares near-term but the broader picture would indicate further gains.
By 1115 GMT, L&G shares were up 6p to 389p.
Shadowing the shares price, L&G's relative strength -- of the share price divided by the All-Share index -- has also fluctuated wildly over the past four months.
But the stock's relative strength line is near its four month low and if the same oscillatory motion is still in force, the shares should make greater gains than the market in general, analysts said.
"The actual (long-term) trend is still in place, and the relative strength confirms this," said Robin Griffiths, technical analyst at HSBC James Capel.
"The latter did lose some momentum in December and January, but now seems to be picking up again," he added.
According to Griffiths, share prices move in discrete or "quantum" steps -- more commonly in multiples of 25 percent and which indicate underlying strength.

"This stock has just passed the 50 percent quantum level from the low (of 266p) last June, and it has done more than 100 percent from the start of 1995 (when the stock price was 170p)," he said. "Stay with the friendly trend."
